content.text:
I opened the four issues, each with an `@pi` line at the end asking for a PR. **No PRs will start on their own, though:** I opened the issues as `pi-action-agent[bot]`, and the `pi-assistant.yml` workflow skips events sent by bots (`github.event.sender.type != 'Bot'`). To start each one, comment `@pi` on the issue yourself.

| Issue | What it asks for |
|---|---|
| #65 Build pi's base system prompt sections (preamble, tools, rules, cwd) | Add pi's opening line, the list of tools, the general rules and the working directory to the system prompt, in pi's order and with pi's text. The tool list follows the tools the model actually gets. |
| #66 Add a `thinking_level` input (default: pi's medium) | Today every run has thinking off. The new input defaults to `medium` like pi, and falls back to `off` for models without reasoning. The release notes should say runs may use more tokens. |
| #67 Support `SYSTEM.md` and `APPEND_SYSTEM.md` | Look the files up the way pi does: project files only with `trust_project`, user files from `agent_dir`. On fork PRs, skip them. Depends on #65. |
| #68 Match pi's context file names and `<project_instructions>` layout | Use pi's file names, in pi's order (`AGENTS.override.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `AGENTS.MD`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.MD`), and pi's layout for the `project_context` section. |

The pi details in the issues come from the source of `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` 1.5.2, not from memory. That includes the exact wording, the order of the sections, the `medium` default, and the trust checks.

A suggested order for starting them:
1. #65 first, because #67 builds on it.
2. Then #67, and #68 after #65 is merged. Both #65 and #68 can change the `project_context` section, so doing them one after the other avoids conflicts.
3. #66 can go at any time; it doesn't touch the system prompt.

No repository files changed.
